articles.title: Foxglove Heights Gets $7,500 for Seasonal Farmers Market
articles.deck: Residents of Foxglove Heights filled the hall on Wednesday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for seasonal farmers market along Yardley Lane, with work expected to start in December.

Theodore Cifuentes, who has lived in Foxglove Heights for 19 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Free Tax Clinic
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting.

To the editor: I have lived on Kiln Drive for 13 years, and I want to say what a difference the Stonebridge Trail Crew has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Please keep the free tax clinic in the budget. Many of us on Kiln Drive use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting.
Ida Sandoval, Canal Park

articles.title: Lorraine Nowicki, 69, Piano Teacher
articles.deck: Friends remember Lorraine Nowicki for the many years of service to Lower Millrace.
body: Lorraine Nowicki died in January at home on Mill Road, at the age of 69. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Lower Millrace.
Born in Lower Millrace in the years after the war, Lorraine Nowicki spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Foxglove Heights Neighbors in his or her name. Lorraine Nowicki died in January at home on Mill Road, at the age of 69.
